body:
Minutes:

- Meeting Logistics and Agenda Adjustments: Johnny Stenback opened the meeting by noting tweaks to the agenda and adjusting meeting schedules for the upcoming Thanksgiving holiday in the United States, indicating that a Europe-friendly meeting would occur the following week before returning to United States time.
- Image Preview Stage One Discussion: Noam Rosenthal raised the topic of advancing image preview to stage one, noting they were happy with stage one, though Microsoft representatives (Olga, Calia, Micola) were absent ([00:01:46](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1B818-GIJBzQvMon3WkbFrCBRpyS61ctOD6N1w34Lu-g/edit?sharingaction=manageaccess&tab=t.z9j85si7pwr0#heading=h.n1pehrlkvlf2)). Johnny Stenback questioned whether it would be an HTML or CSS feature, and Noam Rosenthal responded that they likely did not know yet. Anne van Kesteren noted this did not block stage one, but Simon Pieters expressed that they were not convinced the problem warranted solving, citing Jake's earlier feedback that it might add unnecessary complexity for a temporary problem ([00:03:50](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1B818-GIJBzQvMon3WkbFrCBRpyS61ctOD6N1w34Lu-g/edit?sharingaction=manageaccess&tab=t.z9j85si7pwr0#heading=h.ywb9907t89hu)).
- Poster Element Stage Three Review: Noam Rosenthal requested stage three advancement for poster elements, noting the pull request showed rough consensus on structure despite deep algorithmic defects ([00:03:50](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1B818-GIJBzQvMon3WkbFrCBRpyS61ctOD6N1w34Lu-g/edit?sharingaction=manageaccess&tab=t.z9j85si7pwr0#heading=h.ywb9907t89hu)). Anne van Kesteren and Simon Pieters stated they had not yet reviewed the latest updates, while Scott Jehl joined later to confirm all criteria checkboxes were met and requested feedback to advance ([00:05:16](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1B818-GIJBzQvMon3WkbFrCBRpyS61ctOD6N1w34Lu-g/edit?sharingaction=manageaccess&tab=t.z9j85si7pwr0#heading=h.umirxlxdfazr)) ([00:16:14](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1B818-GIJBzQvMon3WkbFrCBRpyS61ctOD6N1w34Lu-g/edit?sharingaction=manageaccess&tab=t.z9j85si7pwr0#heading=h.t698ralvw13f)). Simon Pieters agreed to review it again ([00:17:21](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1B818-GIJBzQvMon3WkbFrCBRpyS61ctOD6N1w34Lu-g/edit?sharingaction=manageaccess&tab=t.z9j85si7pwr0#heading=h.k3wfsuc8ge5v)).
- Preventing Current Script and Built-In Property Overrides: Simon Pieters discussed investigations using HTTP archive data regarding issue 10687, concluding that web compatibility would improve by preventing legacy overrides on built-in properties like `document.cookie` when a form shares the same name. Simon Pieters reported having a patch for Gecko to remove legacy overrides on documents and noted that Daniel was an expert on clobbering ([00:06:28](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1B818-GIJBzQvMon3WkbFrCBRpyS61ctOD6N1w34Lu-g/edit?sharingaction=manageaccess&tab=t.z9j85si7pwr0#heading=h.tcrg4gf7zqr2)). Anne van Kesteren stated they would slow-follow once the change shipped in stable browsers, while Simon Pieters noted Firefox nightly already implemented a close version ([00:08:20](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1B818-GIJBzQvMon3WkbFrCBRpyS61ctOD6N1w34Lu-g/edit?sharingaction=manageaccess&tab=t.z9j85si7pwr0#heading=h.c9ut39tmufey)).
- Menu Elements and Orientation: David Baron requested further review of the pull request for menu elements now that it reached stage three ([00:08:20](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1B818-GIJBzQvMon3WkbFrCBRpyS61ctOD6N1w34Lu-g/edit?sharingaction=manageaccess&tab=t.z9j85si7pwr0#heading=h.c9ut39tmufey)). Anne van Kesteren inquired about the `is orientation` feature, and David Baron clarified it was absent from both the specification and implementations, though the intent was for the specification to match Chromium's implementation ([00:09:50](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1B818-GIJBzQvMon3WkbFrCBRpyS61ctOD6N1w34Lu-g/edit?sharingaction=manageaccess&tab=t.z9j85si7pwr0#heading=h.hnaszghy2dje)).
- CSS Reading Flow Support: Mason Freed reintroduced pull request 10613 to add support for CSS reading flow, noting it had been open for years, shipped in Chromium, and improved accessibility by aligning tab order and accessibility tree with visual presentation ([00:10:48](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1B818-GIJBzQvMon3WkbFrCBRpyS61ctOD6N1w34Lu-g/edit?sharingaction=manageaccess&tab=t.z9j85si7pwr0#heading=h.kpq3w0u0bt5w)). Anne van Kesteren and Simon Pieters agreed to check internally regarding standard positions and accessibility team concerns raised by Apple to determine what was blocking the feature ([00:11:57](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1B818-GIJBzQvMon3WkbFrCBRpyS61ctOD6N1w34Lu-g/edit?sharingaction=manageaccess&tab=t.z9j85si7pwr0#heading=h.bm6qgk4i3qp6)).
- Changing the Definition of Body Link Colors: Emilio Cobos Álvarez proposed updating the definition of body link colors to use system colors (link text, visited text, and active text) rather than fixed colors, aligning HTML specifications with reality and the implementations of WebKit and Blink ([00:12:43](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1B818-GIJBzQvMon3WkbFrCBRpyS61ctOD6N1w34Lu-g/edit?sharingaction=manageaccess&tab=t.z9j85si7pwr0#heading=h.gvbbn5dey9t)). Emilio Cobos Álvarez noted there would be no compatibility implications, and Anne van Kesteren suggested the change go through the CSS working group or a joint meeting since user agent stylesheets are jointly owned ([00:14:02](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1B818-GIJBzQvMon3WkbFrCBRpyS61ctOD6N1w34Lu-g/edit?sharingaction=manageaccess&tab=t.z9j85si7pwr0#heading=h.nuev4mj4hrl3)). Emilio Cobos Álvarez agreed to submit a pull request with system colors and tests assuming no objections ([00:16:14](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1B818-GIJBzQvMon3WkbFrCBRpyS61ctOD6N1w34Lu-g/edit?sharingaction=manageaccess&tab=t.z9j85si7pwr0#heading=h.t698ralvw13f)).
- Reinstating HTMLDocument: Simon Pieters discussed issue 4792 regarding inconsistencies between HTMLDocument and XMLDocument for XHTML plus XML applications, proposing that Firefox be changed to match Safari and Chrome ([00:17:21](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1B818-GIJBzQvMon3WkbFrCBRpyS61ctOD6N1w34Lu-g/edit?sharingaction=manageaccess&tab=t.z9j85si7pwr0#heading=h.k3wfsuc8ge5v)). Additionally, Simon Pieters proposed removing DOM clobbering for windowless documents as a performance optimization, which Johnny Stenback supported given that clobbering is a legacy feature. Simon Pieters also highlighted an open question regarding named iframes and target attributes in XML documents within Firefox ([00:18:49](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1B818-GIJBzQvMon3WkbFrCBRpyS61ctOD6N1w34Lu-g/edit?sharingaction=manageaccess&tab=t.z9j85si7pwr0#heading=h.yr289a79wnn9)).
- Printing Canvas Elements: Anne van Kesteren raised issue 13223 regarding canvas printing behavior in Chrome upon which Google Docs relies ([00:21:12](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1B818-GIJBzQvMon3WkbFrCBRpyS61ctOD6N1w34Lu-g/edit?sharingaction=manageaccess&tab=t.z9j85si7pwr0#heading=h.7e4wgfgxzp3d)). Emilio Cobos Álvarez explained that Gecko utilizes a `mozPrintCallback` API for vector-based printing, whereas Chrome implicitly records commands when clearing canvases before printing ([00:23:00](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1B818-GIJBzQvMon3WkbFrCBRpyS61ctOD6N1w34Lu-g/edit?sharingaction=manageaccess&tab=t.z9j85si7pwr0#heading=h.f8k9t8hksm4x)). Anne van Kesteren suggested Google representatives consult their canvas team, and Noam Rosenthal agreed to take the issue to the canvas team while keeping the agenda tag active ([00:24:28](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1B818-GIJBzQvMon3WkbFrCBRpyS61ctOD6N1w34Lu-g/edit?sharingaction=manageaccess&tab=t.z9j85si7pwr0#heading=h.xstvccgs0g09)).
- HTML Parsing Consistency for Style and Script Elements: Simon Pieters proposed modifying how style, script, text area, and title elements are parsed within SVG and MathML contexts to completely close mXSS holes for HTML ([00:26:18](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1B818-GIJBzQvMon3WkbFrCBRpyS61ctOD6N1w34Lu-g/edit?sharingaction=manageaccess&tab=t.z9j85si7pwr0#heading=h.flhd8z9skqeg)). Simon Pieters noted this requires a coordinated rollout where server-side serializers and sanitizers are updated before parsers to prevent breaking existing setups, representing a large "boil the ocean" undertaking ([00:27:53](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1B818-GIJBzQvMon3WkbFrCBRpyS61ctOD6N1w34Lu-g/edit?sharingaction=manageaccess&tab=t.z9j85si7pwr0#heading=h.ox24sjz3plxf)) ([00:32:17](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1B818-GIJBzQvMon3WkbFrCBRpyS61ctOD6N1w34Lu-g/edit?sharingaction=manageaccess&tab=t.z9j85si7pwr0#heading=h.k409rppq4tj8)). Anne van Kesteren noted this departs from the original design goal of allowing direct XML copying into HTML streams, but supported proceeding given Simon Pieters' dedication and small XHTML usage rates ([00:29:39](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1B818-GIJBzQvMon3WkbFrCBRpyS61ctOD6N1w34Lu-g/edit?sharingaction=manageaccess&tab=t.z9j85si7pwr0#heading=h.52mp1rv6lxi4)).
- Parser-Aligned Mutation Observer Options: Noam Rosenthal introduced an issue raised by Olli regarding mutation observers and parser alignment creating disordered callbacks and racing issues. Noam Rosenthal presented two options: a parser-aligned observer option on an element where all callback execution waits until parsing finishes, or option two, opting into empty child list observations at parse end ([00:33:50](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1B818-GIJBzQvMon3WkbFrCBRpyS61ctOD6N1w34Lu-g/edit?sharingaction=manageaccess&tab=t.z9j85si7pwr0#heading=h.i4itnz8cy51k)). Noam Rosenthal expressed a personal preference for option two as a lower-level, clearer approach, and Anne van Kesteren noted prior comfort with special child lists at TPAC, leaving final option preferences to be decided offline ([00:35:36](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1B818-GIJBzQvMon3WkbFrCBRpyS61ctOD6N1w34Lu-g/edit?sharingaction=manageaccess&tab=t.z9j85si7pwr0#heading=h.casgv9yvw2eq)).
